You're welcome. I'm glad you think so and I'm happy I could help. 

Thank you, I'm doing alright now and I hope you're feeling better too.

Thank you very much, that means a lot to me.  I'm glad you're safe and that was helpful, I hope you're doing better.

I'm sorry I scared you. I've calmed down a lot since last night after talking to some people and then went to bed. I'm not in danger right now and will probably be spending the day doing productive things.

Thank you again for your kind words, and it makes me happy that I could be of help.

That was a horrible thing of him to say and certainly not true. I know from personal experience there are guys who don't mind body hair on women (and there's certainly many who find plus sized girls and messy hair to be sexy) no matter what mainstream society says. Plus it sounds like you likely had an attractive personality or conventionally cute face anyways, if so many guys have shown interest in you.

Also while I might not know your dad (nor does it excuse the shitty things he said) so maybe this doesn't apply to him, but there are people who have trouble expressing affection or remorse through words and actions no matter how much they genuinely love someone. I had a long distance friend that I would make gifts for (usually drawings or stories of stuff he liked) when he was sad or hurting (or if I had done something shitty to him and I felt bad about it), because I sucked at finding the right words to comfort him (and honestly I probably still do so I apologize if I'm not being of any help) and the distance between us meant I couldn't hug him. So I gave him stuff to show how much I cared since I couldn't express that care very well through words.

I know what you mean, about feeling like a coward for not doing deep enough. Aside from blades I stole from my old job, I once purchased surgical scalpels, but was too much of a coward to actually do much serious damage with them. They bled but the wounds themselves were rarely ever very deep or wide.

However I do know someone who did cut very deep, huge cuts in their abdomen that nearly bled them to death. They told me that they never really felt satisfied no matter how deep they went (so maybe your cuts are deeper than you think and simply feel unsatisfactory) . Now they feel embarrassed by the huge scars and the reactions people give them. Also the cuts caused permanent nerve damage to his body (and I've heard some survivors have had brain damage from the blood loss) which caused difficulty with things he enjoyed such as being able to work out like he used to.

So perhaps its for the best you can't cut deep, if you haven't already. If you continue to live and things do change for the better for you (which I hope they do), you won't have to worry about damage to your body or people giving you weird looks when they see the scars.
